::: {#sol-relu-bends}

Unit $i$ is 0 on one side of $z = -b_i / w_i$ and the line $w_i z + b_i$ on the other,
so its graph is two straight pieces that meet at that point.
A weighted sum of such graphs, plus a constant, is still made of straight pieces,
and can change slope only where some unit does.
So the graph of $\hat{y}$ is a connected chain of straight pieces,
with at most $L$ bends.

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
_ = torch.manual_seed(3)
tiny = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(1, 3), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(3, 1))
z = torch.linspace(-3, 3, 601).unsqueeze(1)
with torch.no_grad():
    y_hat = tiny(z)
    bends = (-tiny[0].bias / tiny[0].weight.squeeze()).numpy()
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.5))
ax.plot(z, y_hat)
for bend in bends:
    ax.axvline(bend, color="gray", linestyle=":")
ax.set_xlabel("z")
ax.set_ylabel("network output")
plt.show()
```

For a random network with $L = 3$, the dotted lines mark the three points $-b_i / w_i$,
and the graph bends at each one that lies in the plotted range.

:::
